input.quote: (ii) the Service will perform in all material respects to industry standards;
input.rationale: Section 9(b) contains a Kubient-given express performance warranty that meets or exceeds the preferred position: the Service will perform in all material respects to industry standards (p0034), services will comply with the Agreement and be free from errors that materially affect their utility (p0038), no viruses/Trojan Horses/worms or other malicious routines (p0036), and compliance with applicable Laws throughout the Term (p0037, p0041). Crucially, these warranties are not time-limited to 12 months/90 days — they run continuously for the Term, which is better for us than the preferred duration. The Section 13 disclaimer does not swallow the express warranty: it applies "Except as expressly set forth herein" and "except for the representations and warranties set forth in this Agreement," so the "as is" language cannot reach Section 9(b); this is not walk-away territory. Noted but not flagged: the Agreement does not spell out the model repair/replace/re-performance/refund remedy mechanic. That is not a material failure here because no clause makes any remedy exclusive or sole, so we retain our full contractual remedies (including damages, subject only to the mutual consequential-damages waiver in Section 7, and indemnification). Importing the model remedy sentence, which is exercisable "at Vendor's option," would in fact narrow our rights, so we should not propose it.
